# aios-kit

`aios-kit` is a lightweight, portable, Agent-friendly installation and distribution kit for a Personal AIOS.

It is not about “installing a few more AI tools.” Instead, it provides a local foundation for your projects, knowledge, services, scripts, skills, and long-running tasks that Agents can understand: humans express goals, Agents develop strategies, the CLI/API performs deterministic actions, and file-based state preserves facts and evidence.

## Current Status

`aios-kit` is still under rapid iteration and is currently in a maintainer preview phase. The public one-click installation entry point has been temporarily withdrawn. Stable installation, upgrade, or cross-platform compatibility is not currently promised to general users.

The installers and installation documentation in this repository are retained as development and validation materials. To evaluate or contribute to the project, first read the [Development Guide](docs/development.md), [Security and Privacy Boundaries](docs/security-and-privacy.md), and [Evolution Roadmap](docs/evolution.md). Begin with source review and a dry run in an isolated environment.

### Evaluate and Install Through an Agent (Recommended Entry Point)

Give the repository link and the following objective to a terminal Agent you trust, such as Hermes, Codex, or Claude Code. The Agent should read the project files and adapt to the current platform rather than blindly copying fixed commands:

```text
Please evaluate and help install aios-kit: https://github.com/LinLin00000000/aios-kit
First read the README and the installation, security, development, and evolution documentation in the repository, and identify the current platform and the boundaries of capabilities that are still under development.
First review the installation scripts and run a dry run. Explain the paths, system configuration, platform limitations, and rollback method that will be affected. Only perform the actual installation after receiving my confirmation.
Do not read, print, or submit secret values, subscription URLs, tokens, keys, or private configuration.
```

## Current Capability Overview

### Core Modules and Directories

| Module / Capability | Installation Location | Default Platform | Purpose | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AIOS instance root | `~/aios` | Linux / Windows; macOS can use dry-run exploration | Consolidates the state, modules, working directories, and cache of a Personal AIOS within a portable boundary | The path can be changed with `--root` |
| `aios-kit` module | `~/aios/modules/aios-kit` | Linux / Windows | Source of the installer, `aios` CLI, skillpack manifest, documentation, and templates | On Linux/WSL, update with `aios update modules` |
| LLL module | `~/aios/modules/lins-living-loop` | Linux / Windows | File-based foundation for long-running tasks and Agent workflows | The module is installed on native Windows; the complete `lll` CLI is currently still recommended on Git Bash/WSL/Linux |
| Command entry points | `~/aios/bin/aios`, `~/aios/bin/lll`; `.ps1/.cmd` shims on Windows | Linux / Windows | Provides stable entry points for Agents and humans without requiring them to remember repository paths | Can optionally be added to PATH |
| Working directory | `~/aios/work` | Designed for all platforms | LLL / Agent working directory for long-running tasks, research, validation, and deliverables | Persistent working layer outside conversations |
| Derived Matter indexes and views | `~/aios/state/matters`, `~/aios/view/matters` | Linux / Windows | Queries active/paused/closed/archived matters across Worksites and presents selected deliverables in read-only form | Can be rebuilt; does not replace Worksite files as the source of truth |
| Configuration / state / logs / cache | `~/aios/config`, `state`, `logs`, `cache` | Designed for all platforms | Stores instance configuration, installation state, logs, and cache | Avoids scattering data across multiple implicit locations |
| Private vault boundary | `~/aios/vault/ops` | Initialized by default on Linux; core directories created on Windows | Stores the OPS vault, a small number of long-term project/Source facts, maintenance records, and other private owner context | Public templates and real private data are kept separate; not all objects need to be registered |
| Runtime skills target directory | `~/.agents/skills` by default, with an optional Hermes target | Full synchronization on Linux / WSL; target initialized first on native Windows | Location where the Agent actually loads skills | Does not take over the entire skills directory; installs managed skills individually |

### `aios` CLI Capabilities

| Command | Purpose | Typical Users |
|---|---|---|
| `aios status` | View a summary of the instance root, vault, work, skills, modules, and other components | Humans / Agents |
| `aios doctor` / `aios doctor --json` | Validate the instance, skillpack, and local asset configuration; JSON mode outputs the versioned `aios.doctor.v1` machine contract | Agent-first |
| `aios update` | Update modules, OPS templates, and managed skills | Agents / Maintainers |
| `aios project ...` | Read and maintain a small number of project facts that require a stable long-term boundary (compatibility entry point; live help still refers to a registry); for ordinary projects, Agents should load local context first rather than requiring prior registration | Agents / Maintainers |
| `aios matter ...` | Rebuild/query derived Matter indexes and Views, and explicitly attach/list/verify registered source materials in read-only mode; see [Matter Lifecycle](docs/matter-lifecycle.md) and [Matter Materials](docs/matter-materials.md) for details | Agent-first |
| `aios lll ...` | Discover, create, open, and inspect LLL workdirs; generate closeout change sets; and use recoverable quarantine instead of direct deletion | Agent-first |
| `aios promotion ...` | Perform dry runs, copy-if-absent operations, validation, and read-only revocation checks for explicitly authorized promotion of long-term assets | Agent-first |
| `aios skillpack ...` | List, synchronize, and inspect managed runtime skills; maintainers can use `adopt` to bring newly created local skills under the Git source of truth | Maintainers / Agents |
| `aios assets ...` | Inspect or link local asset discovery manifests | Maintainers |

The live `aios --help` still describes `project` as “manage the minimal AIOS project registry” and `resource` as resolving existing Project/Source records. These are residual compatibility/read-only binding actuator terms, not a central registry product model.

## Vision and Design Philosophy

The goal of a Personal AIOS is simple: turn AI from a “temporary chat assistant” into an operational layer that can continuously work around your real digital world. It needs to know where projects are located, how services are checked, what the boundaries around data and secrets are, which work can be automated, and which actions require confirmation.

`aios-kit` provides only the minimum skeleton for this operational layer: unified entry points, managed skills, on-demand context loading, necessary long-term facts, an OPS vault, an LLL workflow entry point, and installation/update/check commands. It does not attempt to absorb every tool, nor does it require every project, service, data asset, or capability to first enter a central management table. Instead, it provides different Agents and tools with shared anchors to reality while allowing the actual owners to retain their own context and executors.

Design trade-offs:

| Principle | Trade-off |
|---|---|
| Agent-first | Commands, Skills, the compact catalog, local project context, and vault facts should be easy for Agents to discover, parse, and recover; human commands are a fallback. |
| Management as context engineering | Data assets, servers, services, cloud resources, projects, and capabilities are generally loaded through layered dynamic context rather than being entered into a traditional management platform first; only stable boundaries and security facts are persisted. |
| Official capabilities first | For new integrations, check the official CLI, official Skill, official MCP, and official documentation first; AIOps cards, thin guide Skills, narrow scripts, and traditional APIs follow in that order. |
| Dynamic discovery, precise binding | The Agent semantically selects the owner from candidate context; exact IDs, paths, remotes, versions, and consumers are bound only at the final execution and audit boundary. |
| Files are the source of truth | Important facts that must be recovered across tasks are recorded in owner files, the necessary vault/registry, workdirs, or manifests. Context that can be recovered immediately is not registered redundantly. |
| Thin control plane | `aios` provides context entry points, necessary structural checks, and narrow actuators; LLL, Hermes, Mihomo, and others retain their own state machines. The CLI/API is an Agent actuator, not a set of commands for ordinary users to memorize. |
| Separate private and public data | The public repo contains only templates, scripts, skills, and structure; real assets, secrets, subscriptions, maintenance logs, and local overlays remain in the local vault/state. |
| Progressive evolution | Prioritize breadth across modules while keeping each integration focused; new capabilities must demonstrate that the system complexity they remove is greater than the complexity they introduce. See [docs/evolution.md](docs/evolution.md) for details. |
| Self-iteration | When using AIOS, Agents should proactively propose or record improvements to skills, documentation, the CLI, validation scripts, and workflows when they discover failure patterns, unnecessarily long paths, or validation gaps. |
| Portability over platform lock-in | Default paths should be clear, backed up, and reinstallable; Hermes is the default hub, but not the only Agent. |

Use WSL or a cloud server for complete Linux/server capabilities. |

## Default Directory Structure

```text
~/aios/
  bin/                     # aios / lll command entry points
  config/                  # instance configuration
  vault/ops/               # OPS vault boundary: template structure + private facts entry point
  work/                    # LLL / agent working directory
  skills/                  # AIOS metadata/cache, not the runtime skills directory
  modules/                 # updatable module checkouts
  network/mihomo/          # optional Mihomo network component
  state/ logs/ cache/
```

Runtime skills actually loaded by the Agent are still installed in the Agent's own directory, such as `~/.agents/skills/<skill>` or `~/.hermes/skills/<skill>`. The Linux/WSL backend installs managed skills individually and does not take over the entire skills directory. Native Windows installation currently initializes the skills target directory first; managed skillpack synchronization is still recommended through WSL/Linux.

## LLL Workflow Entry Point

LLL (Lin's Living Loop) is one of the workflow foundations of AIOS, but remains an independent first-class CLI. `aios-kit` is responsible for discovering, installing, updating, and governing LLL; it does not absorb LLL's core state machine.

```bash
./aios update modules lins-living-loop
./aios lll doctor --json
./aios lll list --json
./aios lll new demo --objective "..."
./aios lll status <workdir-or-name> --json
```

The boundary of `aios lll ...` is as follows: by default, it only locates the `lll` CLI/helper, lists LLL workdirs under the AIOS work root, creates new workdirs, or proxies `status`/`validate` to `lll`. Task queues, runners, leases, reapers, and artifacts remain the responsibility of the LLL CLI/protocol. A standard installation exposes both `aios` and `lll` commands in `~/aios/bin/`; `aios lll doctor --json` checks the LLL inside the AIOS module first to avoid being misled by an old version on PATH.

## Networking and Mihomo

The installer first tests external network access without setting proxy environment variables. If direct access fails, the interactive mode asks whether to install Mihomo, with yes as the default; non-interactive `--proxy auto` installs it automatically.

Mihomo is installed to `~/aios/network/mihomo` by default, with TUN enabled by default. On Linux/systemd, it writes an `aios-mihomo.service`. TUN configuration is not universally applicable across Windows/macOS/Linux; current defaults are mainly intended for Ubuntu/Debian cloud servers. See [docs/mihomo-network.md](docs/mihomo-network.md) for details.

## Common Commands

Agents should prioritize JSON/doctor/status probes. Humans should run commands manually only when fallback troubleshooting is required:

```bash
aios status                 # View an instance summary (human-readable)
aios doctor                 # Validate installation and link status (human-readable)
aios doctor --json          # Compact aios.doctor.v1; ok aligns with the exit code, and diagnostic content is centrally redacted
aios update --dry-run       # Preview updates
aios update                 # Update modules, OPS templates, and managed skills
aios update skills          # Refresh managed runtime skills
aios project list           # Compatibility entry point: a small number of long-term project facts (help still says registry)
aios source list            # Compatibility entry point: explicit federated projection of Sources + Projects (help still says federated view)
aios source validate        # Validate Source identity / policy / locator structure
aios lll doctor --json      # Agent-first: check LLL/Code Loop capabilities
aios lll list --json        # Agent-first: enumerate LLL workdirs
```

Maintenance/debugging entry points: `aios skillpack doctor`, `aios skillpack sync --dry-run`, and `aios assets doctor`. If PATH is not configured, use `~/aios/bin/aios status` or `~/aios/bin/lll --version`.
